chapter: Mellophone, Brunswick records and the West End Roof
title: Learning the mellophone and the Brunswick records under Sharkey's name
summary: Hazel explains why he took up mellophone, and that he led the band on his Brunswick sides but hired Sharkey Bonano to record because he lacked nerve.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well I think I was talking about the mellophone when did you start on that and ever play any parades or anything with that?

Yeah I played one parade with Santo. But the mellophone I come to get the mellophone Bill I was having trouble with the conette players. I'd get to play the jazz you know and the conette players would squawk you see. So I said well I'll have to get something that won't interfere. So I remembered Billy Braun playing mellophone with Brownlee see. But he didn't play he played more straight. He didn't play much jazz on mellophone. And the first record I ever made on the mellophone I made with Tony Perini. And I played one note.

And the second time I was I think it was on that record of mine. The Four Sides for Brunswick. The Four Sides for Brunswick yeah. Sizzling and bleeds. Yeah I think I took a break on that. No half a chorus or was it a half a chorus or a break or something.
Yeah one of those four. We made Get With It Ideas, High Society and Sizzling the Bloops. You just played drums on that? I played the upper you see.
I played conette that was my band. See I played conette on that band Bill but I didn't have guts enough to make a record so I hired Sharky. Sharky didn't play with that band.
That's what I wonder. On the label it says.
Yeah I gave him the break under the direction of Sharky Bananas and that's the first record Sharky ever made. What did you do?

Well that was a jazz band. We didn't play anything but jazz up at the roof you see. And I played drums and a conette just like I did later in California with Austin. But when it come to make the record well I didn't have nerve enough. I didn't think I played good enough you know. So I went and got Sharky to make the records with me. But he never did work in that band.
